Implementation.criterion_name: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
Implementation.source_section: Section 3. Quality and efficiency of the implementation

compliance_checklist.description: Scope assessment: The application must correspond, wholly or in part, to the topic description against which it has been submitted. Applications determined to be out of scope must be flagged, reflected in the scoring, and explained in the evaluator comments.
compliance_checklist.source_section: Section 2. Other Questions — Scope of the application

compliance_checklist.description: Assessment of lump sum cost estimations: For lump sum topics, the evaluator must assess the cost estimations and confirm approval or provide recommendations to modify the lump sum budget in the evaluation report. Not applicable for MSCA-PF (unit-cost instrument).
compliance_checklist.source_section: Section 2. Other Questions — Assessment of lump sum cost estimations (additional OPTION for lump sum topics)

compliance_checklist.description: Exceptional funding: A third country participant or international organisation not listed in the General Annex to the Main Work Programme may exceptionally receive funding if their participation is essential to the project (e.g., outstanding expertise, unique know-how, access to research infrastructure, particular geographical environments, key partners in emerging markets, access to data). The evaluator must list participants who should or should not receive exceptional funding and provide justification.

Use of human embryonic stem cells (hESC): The proposal must declare whether it involves the use of hESC. If yes, the evaluator must state whether such use is or is not necessary to achieve the scientific objectives, or flag that it cannot be assessed due to lack of information.
compliance_checklist.source_section: Section 2. Other Questions — Use of human embryonic stem cells (hESC)

compliance_checklist.description: Use of human embryos: The proposal must declare whether it involves the use of human embryos. If yes, the evaluator must confirm an explanation is provided for how human embryos will be used in the project.
compliance_checklist.source_section: Section 2. Other Questions — Use of human embryos

compliance_checklist.description: Activities excluded from funding: The proposal must not include activities that (a) aim at human cloning for reproductive purposes; (b) intend to modify the genetic heritage of human beings (except cancer treatment of the gonads); (c) intend to create human embryos solely for research or stem cell procurement via somatic cell nuclear transfer; or (d) lead to the destruction of human embryos (e.g., for obtaining stem cells). The evaluator must confirm none of these activities are present.
compliance_checklist.source_section: Section 2. Other Questions — Activities excluded from funding

compliance_checklist.description: Exclusive focus on civil applications: The proposed activities must have an exclusive focus on civil applications. Activities intended for military application or that aim to serve military purposes cannot be funded. If the answer is No, an explanation must be provided.
compliance_checklist.source_section: Section 2. Other Questions — Exclusive focus on civil applications
